checks.name: Project & Usage Alignment
checks.notes:
StructuralGeo is an open-source, physics/geometry-based geological simulation package that generates synthetic 3D voxelated subsurface geology volumes by modeling stratigraphic/tectonic processes (e.g., folds, faults, intrusions) to produce training data for downstream generative AI. 
StructuralGeo is used to support Objective (1) by providing the calibrated synthetic data pipeline needed to fine-tune / train a geology foundation model, and it indirectly supports Objective (2) by enabling a generative model that can be used as an AI-based regularizer for physics-based inversion.

checks.name: Project & Usage Alignment
checks.notes:
A large synthetically generated 3D voxel dataset of subsurface geologies, including many volumes at 64×64×64 and 256×256×256 resolution with structures like faults, folds, dikes, and in at least one setup two channels (density + magnetic susceptibility). 
It is used to train / pre-train and later fine-tune the project’s geology foundation model and to support physics-based inversion + mineral exploration / prediction workflows.

checks.name: Training Data Documentation
checks.notes:
publicly available 3D CT scans drawn from datasets including HNSCC, LUNA16, and multiple TCIA CT collections (CT Colonography Trial, COVID-19, LIDC).
The Swin-UNETR model was pretrained on approximately 1,000 synthetically generated 3D geological volumes (256×256×256 voxels, two channels), with random 96³ voxel patches used per step, yielding an estimated D on the order of 10⁸–10⁹ voxel-tokens depending on patch sampling frequency

checks.name: Customisation / Fine-tuning
checks.notes: The pre-trained SwinUNETR encoder is fine-tuned for 3D segmentation benchmarks such as Beyond the Cranial Vault (BTCV) multi-organ CT segmentation and Medical Segmentation Decathlon (MSD) tasks, and MONAI provides examples/tutorials for BTCV and BraTS21-style brain tumor segmentation.

checks.name: Project & Usage Alignment
checks.notes:
flowtrain is a flow-matching generative model (3D attention U-Net architecture with stochastic interpolation) that generates synthetic 3D lithological/subsurface geology volumes, both unconditionally and conditioned on surface topography and sparse borehole observations, for probabilistic subsurface reconstruction.

The architecture preserves U-Net structure with attention blocks at each consecutive stage.

The model directly supports Objective 1 (fine-tuning a foundation model for geology) and Objective 2 (combining generative capabilities with physics-based inversion), specifically serving as the generative prior/foundation model for 3D subsurface reconstruction and aeromagnetic inversion guidance.


Aligns with the approved research topic Datascience and Engineering.

checks.name: Training Data Documentation
checks.notes: The model is trained on synthetically generated 3D voxelated subsurface geology samples produced by the StructuralGeo simulation engine (in-house, not published as a public dataset). The proposal documents two training runs: ~20 million samples at 64×64×64 resolution, and ~1,000 samples at 256×256×256 resolution; the repository's pretrained model used data at 64³ resolution. For Chinchilla D estimation: treating each 3D voxel grid sample as a data point, D ≈ 20,000,000 samples at 64³ (each sample = 262,144 voxels)

checks.notes: A 3D U-Net architecture augmented with attention blocks at each resolution stage, designed for diffusion pretraining and velocity prediction within a stochastic interpolation framework (ODE).

checks.name: Project & Usage Alignment
checks.notes:
GSTools is a geostatistics library for generating spatial random fields, estimating variograms and kriging (interpolating values between sparse observations). It is used to generate and interpolate spatially varying property fields for the project's 3D subsurface models.

It is requested with its two compiled backends:
- gstools_cython 1.2.0, the required default backend
- gstools-core 1.2.0, an optional faster backend written in Rust, used in place of gstools_cython when installed

Aligns with the approved topic, Data Science and Engineering.

addenda.observations:
Change request ticket number: IMS0000203

- 8 new software artifacts reviewed, as listed on the change request form: newer libraries and libraries missing from the original requirements. gstools is reviewed together with its two compiled backends, gstools-core 1.2.0 and gstools_cython 1.2.0.
- emcee and hankel are required dependencies of gstools; lightning requires pytorch-lightning and torchmetrics.
- gstools and its backends are under the LGPL-3.0 license: research use is allowed, and a changed version of these libraries may only be shared under the same license with its source code.
- torchaudio was meant to simulate noise artifacts found in observed data; the group has since dropped it, replacing it with NumPy and SciPy (reply of 3 Nov 2026), so it will not be installed.
- gstools-core 1.2.0 is built from source for GPUP's processor when the image is built.
addenda.recommendation:
The eight software artifacts are non-D5+M and carry no prohibited-use indicators. gstools and its backends are under the LGPL-3.0 license, which allows the project's research use.

monai 1.5.0 carries a critical and several high CVEs, and lightning and pytorch-lightning 2.5.1.post0 carry a high CVE each; all are triggered by loading crafted files or configuration. The group is to load only its own data, checkpoints and configuration files with these libraries.

Recommended for approval.
